items.name: Lauki Sabzi
steps: Wash, trim, and cut the bottle gourd, diced into even pieces.
Warm the ghee in a wide pan; bloom the cumin seeds, then add turmeric.
Add the vegetables and coriander seeds; turn them carefully through the seasoning.
Sprinkle in the water and rock salt, cover, and cook on low heat until tender but not waterlogged.
Uncover for the final minutes, folding gently until excess moisture evaporates and the seasoning clings.
items.guidance: Lauki Sabzi is a softly cooked, moderately seasoned vegetable dish. Vata: cook it fully and add a touch more ghee. Pitta: keep chilies absent and favor coriander. Kapha: reduce fat and leave the finish drier.

items.guidance: This palak paneer uses more spinach than paneer and no cream, keeping the sauce light. Vata: serve warm with the paneer tender. Pitta: keep ginger and salt modest. Kapha: reduce the paneer portion and do not add cream.

items.name: Baingan Bharta
steps: Pierce the eggplant and roast it whole until the skin darkens and the flesh collapses.
Cool just enough to handle, peel away the charred skin, and mash the flesh coarsely.
Warm the ghee, bloom the cumin and ginger, then soften the onion without deeply browning it.
Add tomato, turmeric, and rock salt; cook until the tomato loses its raw edge.
Fold in the mashed eggplant and cook uncovered for eight minutes, stirring until the bharta is soft and cohesive.
items.guidance: Roasting gives this eggplant bharta a soft texture and smoky depth without excessive oil. Vata: add a little ghee and cook the onion fully. Pitta: reduce tomato and ginger. Kapha: retain the light oil measure and serve a modest portion.

items.name: Beans Poriyal
steps: Cut the green beans, finely cut small and evenly so the pieces steam quickly.
Warm the coconut oil; let the mustard seeds pop, then add the curry leaves and turmeric.
Add the vegetables, salt, and water; cover and steam over low heat until just tender.
Remove the lid, fold in the grated coconut, and cook for two minutes without browning it.
Take the pan off the heat while the vegetables retain their color and serve warm.
items.guidance: Beans Poriyal follows the gently steamed vegetable-and-coconut style of southern India. Vata: serve warm and increase coconut slightly. Pitta: keep mustard modest and use the stated coconut. Kapha: reduce coconut and finish the vegetables fairly dry.
provenance: South Indian poriyal and thoran tradition

items.name: Light Vegetable Korma
steps: Soak the cashews for 15 minutes, then grind them with coconut, coriander, and part of the water to a smooth paste.
Warm the ghee, bloom the cumin and ginger, and add the carrot, beans, and cauliflower.
Turn the vegetables for two minutes, add the remaining water and rock salt, and cook covered until nearly tender.
Stir in the coconut-cashew paste and simmer gently for five minutes without boiling hard.
Remove from the heat while the vegetables hold their shape and the sauce remains light.
items.guidance: This vegetable korma uses a restrained coconut-cashew paste and no cream. Vata: serve warm with soft rice. Pitta: keep ginger modest and favor coriander. Kapha: reduce the nut paste and take more vegetables than sauce.

items.name: Avial
steps: Cut all vegetables into even batons so they cook together.
Cook the plantain, carrot, beans, and ash gourd with turmeric, salt, and water until just tender.
Grind the coconut and cumin with a little cooking liquid to a coarse paste and fold it into the vegetables.
Lower the heat completely, stir in the whisked yogurt, and warm gently without allowing it to boil.
Finish with coconut oil and curry leaves, cover for three minutes, and serve warm.
items.guidance: Avial combines tender vegetables with coconut and gently warmed yogurt. Vata: serve warm and keep the vegetables soft. Pitta: use mild yogurt and avoid chilies. Kapha: use less coconut and take a smaller portion.
items.reviewNote: Avial vegetable combinations and the use of yogurt versus raw mango vary by Kerala lineage; this version uses yogurt and only verified linked vegetables.

items.name: Olan
steps: Soak the black-eyed peas for six hours, drain, and simmer them in fresh water until tender.
Blend the grated coconut with part of the measured water and strain to make fresh coconut milk.
Cook the ash gourd with the remaining water and rock salt until translucent and tender.
Fold in the cooked peas and coconut milk; warm gently for four minutes without a hard boil.
Finish with coconut oil and curry leaves, cover briefly, and serve warm.
items.guidance: Olan is a mild ash-gourd and black-eyed-pea preparation enriched with fresh coconut milk. Vata: serve warm and slightly thicker. Pitta: retain the mild seasoning and gentle heat. Kapha: use less coconut milk and a smaller pea portion.

items.name: Kootu
steps: Rinse the pulse and simmer it with turmeric until it begins to soften.
Add the ridge gourd, diced and continue cooking until both pulse and vegetables are tender.
Grind the coconut and cumin with a little cooking liquid to a coarse paste.
Stir the coconut paste and salt into the pot; simmer gently for four minutes without reducing it heavily.
Warm the coconut oil with curry leaves, fold this through the kootu, and rest covered before serving.
items.guidance: Kootu is a mild vegetable-and-pulse preparation thickened with fresh coconut. Vata: serve soft with rice. Pitta: keep the cumin gentle and avoid chilies. Kapha: use less coconut and a smaller serving.
items.reviewNote: Kootu is made with many local gourds; ridge gourd is used here because the canon's snake-gourd key has no exact dravya or store binding.

items.reviewNote: Undhiyu ingredients vary by region and market; this lighter version omits fried dumplings and uses linked green beans in place of unavailable broad beans.

items.name: Sarson Ka Saag
steps: Wash the mustard greens, bathua, and spinach thoroughly and chop them.
Simmer the greens with ginger, garlic, salt, and water until completely tender.
Mash the greens to a rustic puree, leaving a little texture.
Sprinkle in the cornmeal and cook on low heat for eight minutes, stirring so it does not catch.
Finish with warm ghee and serve the saag hot.
items.guidance: Long-cooked winter greens and a little cornmeal give sarson ka saag its characteristic body. Vata: serve with ghee and a soft grain. Pitta: reduce ginger and garlic. Kapha: retain the greens-forward portion and modest ghee.
